brief: Goldman's Hatzius says the AI-driven wealth effect that added about 0.4pp (0.25% of GDP) to US consumer spending growth over the past year is fading just as oil, yields and layoffs turn against 2027. Brent crude near $117 on renewed Gulf escalation fears could range from $75 to $140 depending on how much Gulf oil supply is lost; a roughly 100bp rise in developed-market bond yields since early 2026 could subtract a cumulative 0.6% from GDP if sustained. AI capex keeps rising but its contribution to GDP growth is set to peak near 1.5% of GDP in Q4 and fall to about 0.6% by the end of 2027, with Meta tapping shareholders for up to $95bn after debt markets shut. AI adoption now shows a statistically significant negative correlation with employment growth beyond the tech sector. In a downside scenario where AI stocks fall 40%, the wealth effect flips from a 0.5pp boost to roughly a 0.5pp drag by Q3 2027. Goldman's highest-conviction call is that central banks deliver fewer hikes than priced: one more Fed hike in December, then cuts resuming in late 2027.
